title: Alligator and the rough club in Ponca City
summary: McShann tells of the club in Ponca City, Oklahoma where Indians, whites and blacks mixed and a bouncer called Alligator cleared the room when fights broke out.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: being from Oklahoma, I was exposed to a lot of Indians, and Indians, you know what I mean, you got a chance to see a lot of things, how they did things this way or that way or the other, you know. And in fact, even later years, after I was even trying to play music, you know, I was way up in the northern part of Oklahoma around Ponca City, they've got a lot of those Ponca Indians up there and four or five different tribes, you know, and they used to come in there with the big cowboy boots and hats on and there was a club they used to come in and in fact, everybody used to go there -- white, Indians, black, everybody. You know, they'd get rough in this club, you know.

There was a colored fella that ran this club. They called him Alligator, you know, and he was kind of a rough-looking guy, you know. I guess because he looked like an alligator, you know. I guess that's the reason they called him.

And so, you know, he was kind of rough-looking and I mean, they'd get in there and Alligator would be gone and they'd start fighting and carrying on and somebody would say, 'Go get Alligator.' Alligator would come in there and clean the house completely out. Everybody would go back to their business, if they were shooting the dice or whatever they were doing or if they were drinking the booze or whatever they were

doing. Everything quiet down. "Oh-oh, here comes Alligator." And everything would stop. He was a rough customer, you know, and I'd hate to see Alligator leave because I was in my teens and around there trying to play and I hate to see Alligator leave because they could get pretty rough. They'd come in and put their .45s on the table like that, you know.
